# DriveLaunch

> DriveLaunch is an open-source Android Auto browser built specifically for car head units. Unlike stock Android Auto, which blocks video playback in third-party apps, DriveLaunch plays video content directly through its WebView-based browser — intended for passengers or parked use, not while driving.

Created by Shubham Patel. Licensed under GPLv3.

## What it does

- Provides a launcher-style start page with quick-access tiles to sites and services commonly used in a car (maps, music, video streaming) instead of requiring manual URL entry or bookmark navigation on a car display.
- Plays fullscreen video on Android Auto head units, which the platform normally restricts for built-in streaming apps.
- Supports multiple tabs, bookmarks, a custom home page, and a start page with user-selectable background images.
- Uses a consistent glassmorphism (frosted-glass) UI design system across every screen.
- Is fully responsive across phone, tablet, and car-display screen sizes and orientations.

## Key facts

- Platform: Android, minimum Android 7.0 (API 24), targets Android Auto car displays.
- Language: Kotlin.
- License: GNU General Public License v3.0 (GPLv3) — free and open source.
- Package name: com.shubhampatel.drivelaunch.
